newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends limit-down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends limit-down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended limit-down across the board on Monday on overnight heavy losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
Shanghai's most actively traded December 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 20,410 yuan ($2,462) per tonne, losing 620 yuan. It opened at a high of 20,450.
LME copper prices tumbled during Friday afternoon LME kerb trading to hit their lowest for six months before closing weaker.
The market hit a low of $2,208 before climbing off the floor to end the kerb at $2,213 a tonne, a $58 loss from Thursday.
Shanghai's September fell 620 yuan to 20,200, October 610 to 20,360, November 620 to 20,400, the January 1997 contract 620 to 20,440 and February 650 to 20,500.
Combined volume rose to 81,710 tonnes from 48,020.
Copper opened sharply lower and fell further with all contracts closing limit-down.
Traders said LME losses triggered numerous stop-loss orders, which seriously hurt market sentiment.
"LME losses are the major factor for today's selling because they triggered panic selling," one trader said. "Many investors believe copper will fall further in the next few days."
Physical copper prices were around 20,300 yuan, down sharply from 20,750 at Friday's close due to heavy losses on the futures market, traders said.
They said technical charts showed potential for short term falls after copper breached the support level of 21,000 yuan.
Aluminium ended sharply down, following copper's trend. September fell 350 yuan to 14,300, October 430 to 14,470, November 440 to 14,600 and December 390 to 14,560.
Combined volume rose to 4,280 tonnes from 3,810.
